mainTopic: End of the counting-witnesses discussion; new chapter on joining another's נזירות vow ('And I', husband and wife); ריש לקיש's time limit of תוך כדי דיבור
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier topic: witnesses who disagree about how many terms of נזירות a person vowed. The גמרא asks why רב needed to rule that a disagreement within one pair of witnesses splits their testimony, since he already said so about two separate sets. It then brings the view of ארץ ישראל: a difference in counting is not a contradiction at all, because the smaller number is included in the larger. The chapter then closes with a הדרן, and a new chapter begins. Its משנה teaches that people who hear a נזירות vow and say 'And I' all become נזירים. If the first vow is dissolved, all the vows fall with it, but if the last is dissolved, only the last person is released. Saying 'my mouth is like his mouth and my hair is like his hair' also works. A husband can annul his wife's vow when she joins his, but not when he joins hers. In the גמרא, ריש לקיש requires everyone to join within תוך כדי דיבור, the time of a student's greeting to his רב. רבי יהודה נשיאה objects that this leaves a student no room.

steps.title: Why did רב need to say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's statement as unnecessary. If he ruled this way in the more stringent case, he would surely rule the same way in the more lenient case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this? Now, can it be said that רב stated the stringent case but would not say the lenient one?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking why רב bothered to state a ruling that seems obvious from something he already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב said that even two separate sets of witnesses who disagree have their testimony treated as divided. That is the 'stringent' case, because full sets of witnesses are normally strong. So it seems obvious that a disagreement inside a single pair, the 'lenient' case, would be treated the same way. That makes the extra statement look pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this? (the statement seems unnecessary)
Now, considering that (introduces a 'how much more so' argument)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'stringent' and 'lenient' describe how strong the case for treating the testimony as divided is. They are not about being strict or easy in practice.

phrases.english: Why do I need this?
phrases.notes: He means: why did רב need to state this ruling at all?

phrases.english: Now, can it be said:
The stringent case רב stated,
phrases.notes: This is the case of two separate sets of witnesses who disagree.

phrases.english: The lenient case he would not state?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לְמָה לִי? הַשְׁתָּא יֵשׁ לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רב's ruling on witnesses who disagree about a count of נזירות terms.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling about a disagreement within one set of witnesses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 'how much more so' argument: whatever applies to the stronger case of two sets applies even more to one set, so the extra statement is unnecessary.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל they say a counting difference is not a contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of ארץ ישראל teach that when witnesses differ in a count, they do not truly contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say in the West: there is no contradiction in counting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a saying from ארץ ישראל that changes how we look at witnesses who give different numbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose one witness says the person vowed two terms of נזירות and the other says five. The smaller number fits inside the larger one, so the two statements do not truly clash. That is why counting cases are not treated like ordinary contradicting testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: A difference in number is not a real contradiction, because the smaller number is included in the larger one.

phrases.english: They say in the West:
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל.

phrases.english: There is no contradiction in counting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the discussion raised in step 1 by changing how counting disagreements are viewed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the case: a difference in number is not a contradiction at all
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Witnesses who give different numbers seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Different numbers do not clash, because the smaller is included in the larger.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter מי שאמר
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'מי שאמר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter ends here with the traditional farewell line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן expresses our wish to come back and learn this chapter again. Nothing new is taught; it simply marks the end of the chapter.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said at the end of a chapter)

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'One who said'

steps.title: Joining someone's vow by saying 'And I'
steps.stepSummary: If one person vows נזירות and others hear it and say 'And I,' they all become נזירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone said 'I am hereby a נזיר,' and another heard and said 'And I,' and another said 'And I,' they are all נזירים.
steps.whatsHappening: The new chapter's משנה opens. It teaches that a person can take on נזירות just by attaching himself to someone else's vow with the words 'And I.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The listeners never say the word 'נזיר' themselves. Still, 'And I' is enough to tie them to the first person's words, so each of them is fully bound.

keyTerms.meaning: I am hereby a נזיר (the vow formula)
And I (joining the vow just made)
People bound by a נזירות vow

phrases.english: One who said: 'I am hereby a nazirite'
and his fellow heard and said: 'And I,'
'And I' — they are all nazirites.
phrases.notes: This second 'And I' is said by a third person who joins in.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁאָמַר הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר וְשָׁמַע חֲבֵירוֹ וְאָמַר וַאֲנִי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'And I' after someone's נזירות vow makes the speaker a נזיר as well.

steps.title: Dissolving the first vow or the last vow
steps.stepSummary: If the first vow is dissolved, every vow that hangs on it falls away. If the last vow is dissolved, only the last person is released.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the first was released, all are released. If the last was released, the last is permitted and all the others remain bound.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what happens when a חכם releases one person in the chain of vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each 'And I' rests on the vow said before it. When the first vow is dissolved, it is as if it never existed, so there was nothing for the others to join. The last person's vow, though, holds nobody else up, so releasing him affects only him.

keyTerms.meaning: Was released (a vow dissolved by a חכם)

steps.confusionAlert: הותר here means a חכם dissolving the vow from the start. It is not the same as a husband's הפרה, which comes up later in the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the later vows depend on the first one, an idea that drives the husband-and-wife cases below.

phrases.english: If the first was released — they are all released.
If the last was released —
the last is permitted and all the others are bound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the chain of vows created in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dissolving the first vow cancels all the vows that depend on it. Dissolving the last vow releases only the last person.

steps.title: 'My mouth is like his mouth'
steps.stepSummary: Saying 'my mouth is like his mouth and my hair is like his hair' also makes the listener a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one said 'I am hereby a נזיר,' and his fellow heard and said 'My mouth is like his mouth and my hair is like his hair,' he is a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another wording that works for joining someone's נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These words point to the main limits of a נזיר: what he may not drink (the mouth) and the hair he may not cut. Comparing himself to the first נזיר in these ways is enough to make him a נזיר too.

keyTerms.meaning: My mouth is like his mouth
My hair is like his hair

phrases.english: One said: 'I am hereby a nazirite,'
and his fellow heard and said:
'My mouth is like his mouth and my hair is like his hair' —
this one is a nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another way of joining a vow, alongside 'And I.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Comparing one's mouth and hair to a נזיר's makes the speaker a נזיר.

steps.title: The wife joins her husband's vow
steps.stepSummary: If the husband vows and the wife says 'And I,' he may annul her vow, and his own vow stays in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'I am hereby a נזיר,' and his wife heard and said 'And I,' he annuls hers, and his remains.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now applies the 'And I' rule to a husband and wife, where the husband has the power of הפרה over his wife's vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her vow rests on his, but his vow does not rest on hers. So he can use his power of הפרה on her vow, and his own נזירות is not touched.

keyTerms.meaning: Annuls (a husband cancelling his wife's vow)

phrases.english: 'I am hereby a nazirite,' and his wife heard
and said: 'And I' —
he annuls hers, and his remains in force.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר וְשָׁמְעָה אִשְׁתּוֹ וְאָמְרָה וַאֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'And I' rule to a husband and wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the wife joins her husband's vow, he may annul hers, and his own remains.

steps.title: The husband joins his wife's vow
steps.stepSummary: If the wife vows and the husband says 'And I,' he can no longer annul her vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she said 'I am hereby a נזירה,' and her husband heard and said 'And I,' he cannot annul.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the case: now the wife vows first and the husband joins her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His vow now rests on hers. Annulling her vow would also pull out the base of his own vow, and he has no power to cancel his own vow. By joining her, he has in effect confirmed her vow.
steps.confusionAlert: Compare this with step 7. Who vowed first decides whose vow depends on whose, and that decides whether he can annul.

phrases.english: 'I am hereby a nazirite,' and her husband heard
and said: 'And I' —
he cannot annul.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵינִי נְזִירָה וְשָׁמַע בַּעֲלָהּ וְאָמַר וַאֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse of step 7, with the opposite result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband who joins his wife's vow cannot annul it.

steps.title: 'I am a נזיר, and you' — she answers 'Amen'
steps.stepSummary: If the husband includes his wife in his vow and she accepts with 'Amen,' he may annul hers, and his own remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'I am hereby a נזיר, and you,' and she said 'Amen,' he annuls hers, and his remains.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another form of joining: one spouse includes the other, and the other accepts by saying אמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying אמן is like accepting the vow on oneself. Her vow comes through his, but his does not depend on hers, so the result matches step 7.

phrases.english: 'I am hereby a nazirite, and you,' and she said: 'Amen' —
phrases.notes: 'And you' means: and you shall be a נזירה too.

phrases.english: he annuls hers, and his remains in force.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the rule of step 7 using 'and you' plus אמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the husband includes his wife and she answers אמן, he may annul hers.

steps.title: 'I am a נזירה, and you' — he answers 'Amen'
steps.stepSummary: If the wife includes her husband in her vow and he accepts with 'Amen,' he cannot annul her vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she said 'I am hereby a נזירה, and you,' and he said 'Amen,' he cannot annul.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with the reverse of the 'Amen' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By answering אמן, the husband bases his own vow on hers. Just as in step 8, he cannot cancel her vow without also undoing his own.
steps.whatToRemember: Whoever joins the other's vow, whether by 'And I' or by אמן, is depending on it. A husband who joins his wife's vow loses his power to annul it. A husband whose wife joins his vow keeps that power.

phrases.english: 'I am hereby a nazirite, and you,' and he said: 'Amen' —
he cannot annul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse of step 9, matching the result of step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband who accepts his wife's 'and you' with אמן cannot annul her vow.

steps.title: Everyone must join the vow within a few seconds
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, sitting before רבי יהודה נשיאה, rules that the people saying 'And I' only become נזירים if they all joined within תוך כדי דיבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: ריש לקיש was sitting before רבי יהודה נשיאה, and as he sat he said: This rule applies only when all of them attached themselves to the vow within תוך כדי דיבור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. ריש לקיש adds a time limit: saying 'And I' only works if it is said right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that each person who says 'And I' becomes a נזיר. ריש לקיש narrows this rule: the joining only counts if it happens within a very short window, תוך כדי דיבור. A delayed 'And I' is too disconnected from the original vow to attach to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion that follows the משנה
An אמורא from ארץ ישראל, also called רבי שמעון בן לקיש
רבי יהודה the נשיא, a grandson of רבי
They attached or connected themselves to someone else's vow
Within the short time of a brief utterance, treated as one continuous statement

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of תוך כדי דיבור appears throughout שס. Something said within that tiny window counts as part of the original statement.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Reish Lakish was sitting
before Rabbi Yehuda Nesia
and as he sat he said:
This applies only when all of them attached themselves
phrases.notes: 'This' means the משנה's rule that everyone who says 'And I' becomes a נזיר.

phrases.english: within the time of an utterance.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא שֶׁהִתְפִּיסוּ כּוּלָּן בְּתוֹךְ כְּדֵי דִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a time condition to the משנה's rule about joining a vow by saying 'And I.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Joining another's נזירות by saying 'And I' works only if done within תוך כדי דיבור.

steps.title: How long is 'within the time of an utterance'?
steps.stepSummary: The time of תוך כדי דיבור is defined as the time of a greeting, and specifically as the time it takes a student to say 'שלום' to his רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how long is תוך כדי דיבור? The time of a greeting. And how long is a greeting? The time it takes a student to greet his רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks two follow-up questions to measure the time limit exactly. The answer is the length of a student's short greeting to his רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, תוך כדי דיבור is set as the time of שאלת שלום, a greeting. Since greetings vary in length, a second question pins it down: a student's greeting to his רב, which the classic sources give as 'שלום עליך רבי'. That gives a fixed and very short window of time.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the time of a long, chatty greeting. It is the few words a student says to greet his רב, only a couple of seconds.

phrases.english: And how long is the time of an utterance?
The time of a greeting.
And how long is the time of a greeting?
The time it takes to say 'Shalom,'
by a student to his teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the time limit that step 11 introduced.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact length of תוך כדי דיבור.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The time it takes a student to say 'שלום' to his רב.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה protests that the student is left no room
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה objects that this short time limit leaves no room for a student who wants to join the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה נשיאה said to him: Once again you have left no room for a student!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה נשיאה pushes back on ריש לקיש's tiny time limit. He says it is unfair to a student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a student's רב happens to pass by just as someone vows, the student must greet his רב first. That greeting uses up the whole window of תוך כדי דיבור, so the student can no longer say 'And I' in time.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: joining a vow with 'And I' must happen within תוך כדי דיבור, the time of a student's greeting to his רב. רבי יהודה נשיאה objects that this leaves a student no room.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה נשיאה is speaking to ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Once again you have not left
any room for a student!
phrases.notes: If his רב walks by, the student must greet him first, and by then the time to say 'And I' has run out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the short time limit defined in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's measure of תוך כדי דיבור as a student's greeting to his רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The window is so short that a student who must first greet his passing רב would miss the chance to join the vow.
